constructions.title: Stations classified by the brief's seasonality convention

all_nine.stations.is: Stations of the monthly station series with at least one station-month on any of the nine variables.

all_nine.seasonal.is: Stations classed seasonal: Z above `z_cut` and mean direction in June to September, where N counts the station's station-months over the nine variables pooled, so a month is counted once for each variable reported in it.

all_nine.year_round.is: Stations classed year-round on the same pooled basis: Z at or below `z_cut` and N at least `min_n`.

all_nine.neither.is: Stations in neither class on the pooled basis, those with too few observations among them.

oxy_bed.stations.is: Stations with at least one station-month of `oxy_bed`, near-bed oxygen.

oxy_bed.seasonal.is: Stations classed seasonal on `oxy_bed` alone, one observation per station-month.

oxy_bed.neither.is: Stations in neither class on `oxy_bed` alone.

oxy_bed.at_least_min_n.is: Stations with at least `min_n` station-months of `oxy_bed`: those a year-round class could hold.

oxy_bed.raw_r_group.is: Stations whose mean resultant length R on `oxy_bed` exceeds `raw_r_cut`, with no minimum N: the raw-R rule the convention replaces.

oxy_bed.raw_r_single.is: Stations of that raw-R group with exactly one station-month.

oxy_bed.raw_r_at_most_three.is: Stations of that raw-R group with at most three station-months.

constructions.what: The brief's station seasonality convention applied to every station of the monthly station series, on the nine variables pooled and on near-bed oxygen alone, with the counts of the raw-R rule without a minimum that it replaces.
constructions.model: Each station-month in `stations_series.bin` becomes a unit vector at the angle of its calendar month, $\theta = 2\pi m / 12$ with `m = month_index % 12`. For a station with N vectors, $R = |\sum_k e^{i\theta_k}| / N$ and $Z = N R^2$; the mean direction is the angle of the sum, rounded to the nearest month. Seasonal: `z > z_cut` and the mean month in June to September; year-round: `z <= z_cut` and `n >= min_n`; neither otherwise (`classify()` in `scripts/pages/agent_brief.py`). The raw-R group is `r > raw_r_cut` with no minimum.
assumptions: The series' month index counts months from January of `year0`, so its remainder modulo twelve is the calendar month.

An observation is one station-month of the series, which holds a monthly median per station: repeated casts within a month count once. On the nine-variable basis a station-month counts once for each variable, a reading of the convention chosen because under it, and not with the months merged across variables, the counts the brief first printed come out the same.

justified.text: Every station-month of every variable in the series is read, one variable block at a time, and each station is classified by the rule the brief states, with its cut, minimum and season as constants beside the stated values the page prints.
The series is the monthly station panel the project's partition and composition analyses read; its header gives the byte layout the reader follows.

gaps: Rounding the mean direction to the nearest month decides stations whose mean falls near the edge of June or September; no other rounding is tested.
The nine-variable basis weights a station by how many variables it reports as well as by how often it was visited.
void_if: the station series is rebuilt with a different month index or unit
the convention's cut, minimum or season changes without the page's wording following
constructions.licenses: How many stations of the series fall in each class under this convention, and how the raw-R rule without a minimum behaves on `oxy_bed`.
constructions.not_licensed: Anything about the seasonality of the sea: the class describes when a station was observed, not what it observed.

constructions.title: Outfalls reporting a reduced impervious area

layers.*.totals.Red areal.n.is: Features of one layer of the spildevandsdata.dk PULS extract whose `Red areal` property is a number; a reported zero counts.

constructions.what: For each outfall layer, how many features carry a numeric reduced impervious area.
constructions.model: `numeric()` in `scripts/fetch_spildevand.py` keeps every property value that is a number, or a string that parses as one once spaces are removed and a decimal comma is read, and skips booleans and missing values; `n` is the count kept. A field is summarised only when more than `0.3` of the features carry it and one value at least is non-zero.
assumptions: A reduced area a utility reports as zero is a reported value, not a missing one.

justified.text: The count is taken over every feature of the fetched layer, and the EXPERIMENTS page refuses to build unless it equals the layer's feature count.

gaps: The reduced areas are reported by the utilities through PULS; how each was derived is not documented in the extract, and some of them are zero.
void_if: the layers are refetched with a different field set
constructions.licenses: That every feature of the combined-overflow and separate-stormwater layers carries a reduced-area value.
constructions.not_licensed: That the values are measured, non-zero or comparable between utilities.
